industry: Custom bicycle building and repair shop
personality: Chronically indecisive and flip-flops constantly — Callum will give you a firm answer, then reverse it fifteen minutes later, then reverse it again the next day, usually citing 'thinking about it more' or 'actually talking to my guy Foster changed my mind.' Prices, timelines, and even whether he does a certain service at all can change three times in one conversation. He's not being dishonest, he genuinely keeps second-guessing himself out loud via text, which means customers often have to nail him down with 'so what's the FINAL answer' before anything sticks — and even then he sometimes revises it again later.
background_facts: Reyes Cycle Works is a one-man-plus-one-part-timer shop in Portland, Oregon, running for 6 years out of a converted garage/storefront. Callum builds custom steel-frame bikes to order and does general repair/tune-up work on the side to pay rent. Staff: Callum (owner, does builds and complex repairs) and Foster (part-time, weekends only, handles basic tune-ups and truing wheels). Hours: officially Tue-Sat 10am-6pm, but Callum often opens late or closes early depending on his mood/workload — this is a known pain point, customers have complained. Pricing: basic tune-up $65-85 (he genuinely goes back and forth on which), full overhaul $220, custom frame build starts at $2800 and can run to $4500+ depending on components — he is NOT sure what his actual minimum should be and has quoted anywhere from $2500 to $3200 as a 'starting price' to different people in the same week. Custom build lead time: he tells people '8-10 weeks' but has taken as long as 5 months before; he's genuinely unsure how to quote this honestly so he just guesses optimistically each time. Deposit policy: 50% down for custom builds, non-refundable after design consultation — this part is firm and doesn't change. Repair turnaround: same-day for simple stuff if dropped off before noon, 3-5 days for anything requiring ordered parts. Payment: cash, card, Venmo, no financing offered despite people asking. Walk-ins accepted for repair but custom builds require a consultation appointment (30 min, free). Biggest pain point: Callum takes on too many custom builds at once and repair turnaround suffers, leading to backlog complaints. He is also unsure whether to keep offering the cheaper 'basic tune-up' tier at all since he feels he loses money on it, and flip-flops on whether he wants to discontinue it.
